blocks.text: Why your social media manager link in bio fails to convert

Many social media managers treat the link in bio as a static placeholder. They often link to a generic homepage instead of a focused landing page. This forces the user to search for the product or service themselves. Users rarely have the patience for this extra step. If you make them work for it, they will leave.

Another common mistake is inconsistent branding. If your Instagram post uses a specific color palette and tone, but your landing page looks completely different, the user will feel lost. This disconnect creates friction. Friction is the enemy of conversion.
Costs of low conversion for social media managers

Poor conversion rates represent lost revenue and wasted effort. You spend hours creating content, only to lose the audience at the final step. This cycle leads to burnout. You feel like you are shouting into a void because the metrics never move.
How to fix your conversion path without buying new tools

items: Audit your landing page on your Mac using Safari's responsive design mode. Go to Develop > Enter Responsive Design Mode to see how it looks on mobile.
Remove unnecessary navigation links from your landing page. Keep the user focused on a single action.
Match the headline of your landing page to the hook in your social post.
Add a clear, high-contrast button for your main goal.
Use free heatmapping tools to see exactly where users stop scrolling.
